A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cross-LiDAR occupancy prediction work, renamed from UniLiDAR to MergeOcc. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy prediction, cross-dataset transfer, and component-ablation results on OpenOccupancy-nuScenes and SemanticKITTI, including appendix experiments and visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds semantic-label-mapping and single-dataset range-alignment comparisons in Table 4 and Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: Both versions describe minimum-range alignment, dataset-specific normalization, shared backbone and separate heads, combinatorial semantic label mapping, and coarse-to-fine prediction. Semantic label mapping already appears in v1 Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1; its additional evaluation in v2 does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate occupancy prediction on OpenOccupancy-nuScenes and SemanticKITTI, representing 32-beam and 64-beam LiDARs. The added range-alignment control reuses this coverage; no additional dataset, task, or deployment domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark tables retain the same comparator sets, including PointOcc on OpenOccupancy-nuScenes and SCPNet on SemanticKITTI. Single-dataset, pre-training, and direct-merging baselines also remain. Newly cited work in the semantic-mapping discussion is not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 Table 6 adds a controlled comparison of range alignment under single-dataset versus joint training. Existing experiments retain the documented ranges, splits, metrics, 24-epoch budget, batch size, and LiDAR sweep counts. The new statement that baseline hyperparameters were retained is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 Table 4 adds G.R.+SLM against the retained G.R. configuration, isolating the existing semantic-mapping component. Appendix A.3 adds a range-alignment control testing whether alignment alone explains improvements. These are targeted extensions; the earlier normalization-scope analysis remains unchanged in Table 7.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 newly states that results on both datasets average three experiments; v1 provides no corresponding run-count statement. This establishes newly reported averaging, not an increase in runs. Neither version reports seeds, dispersion, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3's proposed-model IoU/mIoU changes from 38.4/21.4 to 40.2/22.9, with revised class scores including bicycle 57.0 to 8.8. SemanticKITTI IoU changes from 69.9 to 70.1, retaining 14.5 mIoU. v2 separately identifies G.R.+SLM and retains the earlier G.R. scores, so these are not established same-configuration gains. Table 2 also revises Align Min scores, and Table 6 adds single-dataset alignment results.

T1.justification: The normalization formula, Boolean mapping constraints, matching/ILP formulation, complexity argument, Algorithm 1, and coarse-to-fine derivation are retained. The separate dataset-specific loss equation is consolidated into the retained joint objective. Notation and equation numbering change without a substantive theoretical addition.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the repeated continual-learning claim with simultaneous cross-LiDAR occupancy prediction. v2 also elevates improvement with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and the claimed insufficiency of individual datasets, into explicit contributions. This materially revises the central framing while retaining the alignment-based approach.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its new control as showing that range alignment benefits depend on joint training, attributing gains principally to broader data. It adds duplicate-output redundancy as motivation for semantic mapping and explains the two-dataset selection. The inability to handle unseen LiDARs was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that OpenOccupancy hyperparameters were retained without modification. Appendix A.1 replaces v1's direct anonymous code URL with an unspecified supplementary-material reference. The earlier in-domain/out-of-domain head-selection explanation is omitted, while most implementation details remain available after relocation to Appendix A.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2019), Towards Universal Object Detection by Domain Attention, to its semantic-mapping comparison and removes several general detection/segmentation references with the broader perception survey. Positioning against Uni3D and Zhou et al. remains. Zhao et al. (2020) completes v1's existing reference rather than adding a new work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution presentation, related work, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Experimental settings move into Appendix A.2, semantic-disparity examples move into Appendix A.6, and appendix sections are reorganized. The UniLiDAR-to-MergeOcc renaming accompanies substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensively resized and restyled figures and tables. Figure 1 gains difference annotations, Table 1 gains ground-truth ranges, the SemanticKITTI table moves to the appendix, and a new control table appears. Figure 5 replaces an earlier scene with a duplicate of an existing example.

improvement.justification: The explicit SLM comparison in Table 4 and range-alignment control in Table 6 strengthen evidence for the existing framework and its interpretation. The revised framing better matches the joint-training experiments, and three-experiment averaging is now disclosed. Less specific code access and the duplicated Figure 5 example weaken the revision, but the targeted validation gains support a modest net improvement.
